descriptionEN: Europeans regard the European Union as a place of stability in a troubled world, according to the Spring 2026 Eurobarometer. They value its peaceful, protective and cooperative nature, and recognise the quality of life it enables. However, economic concerns, particularly regarding the cost of living, have increased over recent years, and the overall mood of citizens fluctuates between uncertainty and hope. The Eurobarometer shows many trends already present in past surveys. However, some indicators reflect the immediate reactions of Europeans to recent disruptions in the global political and economic climate.

themes.description: EU institutions and European civil service

titleEN: Attractiveness of Vocational Education and Training
descriptionEN: The Special Eurobarometer on the attractiveness of Vocational Education and Training (VET) highlights citizens’ positive views on VET as a pathway to well-paid jobs and opportunities – but the overall image of VET lags behind.

The risk of cyberbullying or harassment that children face on social media (mentioned by 71% of respondents) and the risk of online grooming or sexual exploitation that children face on social media (70%) are the biggest concerns of Europeans. To further strengthen the protection of children online, 36% of Europeans think the EU should adopt EU-level rules that prohibit social media providers from offering their services to children below a certain age while 27% think the EU should adopt EU-level rules that oblige social media providers to delay offering access to certain unsafe social media to children below a certain age. For Europeans, freedom of speech / expression (34%), free and fair elections (32%) and respect for the rule of law and protection of fundamental rights (31%) are the most important elements of a democratic society. Over two thirds (68%) agree that the EU should strengthen its capacity to defend itself autonomously against potential external threats and 56% trust the European Union to strengthen security and defence in Europe and better protect its citizens. Over half (56%) say that developing more renewable energy capacity through e.g. new wind farms and solar parks can help the EU to transition away from fossil fuels.

titleEN: Introduction of the euro in the Member States that have not yet adopted the common currency
descriptionEN: A majority of citizens (57%) in the EU Member States that have yet to adopt the euro think that the common currency has had a positive impact on those countries that already use it. A majority also believe that introducing the euro would have positive consequences for their own country (51%) and for them personally (52%). Over half of respondents (52%) are in favour of introducing the euro in their country. Support is especially pronounced in Hungary (80%) and Romania (65%), followed by Sweden (51%), Poland (43%) and Czechia (42%).
The Special Eurobarometer on the Digital Decade 2026 presents European citizens' views and opinions on key aspects of the digital transformation in the 27 EU Member States.
